title: Taxonomic Classification

standard_text: Living things are classified into domains and kingdoms and named with binomial nomenclature; taxonomic ranks from kingdom to species; dichotomous keys. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 2, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free JSS 2 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): taxonomy and scientific names, domains and kingdoms, bacteria, viruses and protists, fungi and plants and animals and biodiversity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things are grouped by shared features and evolutionary history.
key_sub: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.
body_html:
How to think about it

Biologists sort the huge variety of life into groups that share features and ancestry. The ranks go from broad to narrow: domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species. Every species has a two-part scientific name, the genus and the species, written in italics (Acer saccharum, the sugar iroko).

The three domains are Bacteria, Archaea (both prokaryotes, with no nucleus) and Eukarya (cells with a nucleus). Eukarya includes protists, fungi, plants and animals. Viruses are not placed in any kingdom: they are not cells and can only reproduce inside a host cell.

Example

Which two ranks make up a scientific name?

Binomial nomenclature uses the genus and the species.

Answer: genus and species

Example

A cell has no nucleus and lives in a hot spring. Which domains are possible?

No nucleus means prokaryote.

Answer: Bacteria or Archaea

Common mistakes

  • Writing the genus with a small letter or not using italics.
  • Calling viruses bacteria: viruses are not cells.
  • Thinking that fungi are plants: fungi do not photosynthesise and have chitin cell walls.

items.q: What is the common name of Mangifera indica?
items.e: Mangifera indica: mango.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 5, species B 12, species C 5, species D 4. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above genus?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: In Mangifera indica, what does 'indica' stand for?
items.e: Mangifera is the genus.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for wheat?
items.e: Triticum aestivum: wheat.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for cotton?

Which category includes related genera?
items.e: e.g. Felidae includes Panthera and Felis.

items.q: Why is growth not a defining property of living things?
c: non-living things such as mountains and crystals can also grow by accumulation
items.e: Growth in living things is from inside.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above family?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: Which bacteria produce methane (biogas) in the guts of cows?
items.e: They are archaebacteria.

items.q: Which is the correct order from the highest to the lowest category?
c: kingdom, class, phylum, order, family, genus, species
kingdom, phylum, order, class, family, genus, species
species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom
kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
items.e: Remember: King Philip Came Over For Good Soup.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Monera?
c: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
items.e: Monera: prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan.

items.q: Which protists cause red tides?
items.e: They can release toxins that kill fish.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food?
items.e: Plantae: multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food.

items.q: What are viroids?
c: free RNA without a protein coat that cause disease
items.e: Found by T. O. Diener; cause potato spindle tuber disease.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are euglenoids, with a pellicle and a flagellum?
items.e: Euglena photosynthesises in light.

items.q: Who proposed the five-kingdom classification?
items.e: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia (1969).

items.q: Which taxonomic aid is information about any one taxon?
items.e: monograph: information about any one taxon.

items.q: What is the cell wall of diatoms made of?
items.e: Their deposits form diatomaceous earth.

items.q: Which are the smallest living cells and have no cell wall?
items.e: They can survive without oxygen.

items.q: Which is the basic unit of classification?
items.e: Members can interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

items.q: What is a monograph?
c: a tool that identifies organisms using pairs of contrasting characters
a garden of living plants grown and labelled for study
a place where wild animals are kept in protected surroundings like their natural habitat
items.e: monograph: information about any one taxon.

items.q: What is a flora?
c: an account of the plant species found in an area
a place where wild animals are kept in protected surroundings like their natural habitat
a garden of living plants grown and labelled for study
items.e: flora: an account of the plant species found in an area.

items.q: What are prions?
c: abnormally folded proteins that cause disease
items.e: e.g. mad cow disease (BSE).

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food?
items.e: Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Plantae?
c: prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food
heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
items.e: Plantae: multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Animalia?
c: prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
items.e: Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are unicellular eukaryotes?
items.e: Protista: unicellular eukaryotes.

items.q: Which taxonomic aid is a tool that identifies organisms using pairs of contrasting characters?
items.e: key: a tool that identifies organisms using pairs of contrasting characters.

items.q: What are heterocysts in cyanobacteria used for?
items.e: e.g. Nostoc and Anabaena.

items.q: What is a lichen?
c: a symbiotic association of an alga and a fungus
items.e: They are pollution indicators.

items.q: How is HIV spread?
c: sexual contact and exchange of body fluids
items.e: Know how to stop the spread.

items.q: What type of pathogen causes tobacco mosaic virus (TMV)?
items.e: Viruses, bacteria, fungi and protists.

items.q: How is malaria spread?

items.e: Know how to stop the spread.

items.q: What type of pathogen causes gonorrhoea?
items.e: Viruses, bacteria, fungi and protists.

items.q: How is gonorrhoea spread?

items.e: Know how to stop the spread.

items.q: Why are fungi called saprophytes?
c: they absorb food from dead and decaying matter
items.e: They are important decomposers.

a thick yellow or green discharge and pain when urinating
items.e: Symptoms help diagnosis.

items.q: What is the main drawback of the two-kingdom classification?
c: it puts prokaryotes and eukaryotes, unicellular and multicellular, together
items.e: Bacteria, fungi and plants were all in Plantae.

items.q: What is the genetic material of bacteriophages usually?
items.e: Plant viruses usually have single-stranded RNA.

items.q: What is the endosperm of gymnosperms?
items.e: There is no double fertilisation.

items.q: To which class of fungi do Penicillium, Aspergillus and yeast belong?
items.e: Ascomycetes: Penicillium, Aspergillus and yeast.

items.q: In which group do vascular tissues first appear?
items.e: They have true roots, stems and leaves.

items.q: Which fungi belong to Deuteromycetes?
items.e: Deuteromycetes: Alternaria and Trichoderma.

items.q: What is the tallest tree species?
items.e: Some are over 100 m tall.

items.q: To which class of fungi do Rhizopus and Albugo belong?
items.e: Phycomycetes: Rhizopus and Albugo.

items.q: Which gymnosperm has coralloid roots with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria?
items.e: Pinus has mycorrhiza instead.

items.q: Which group of plants is described as gymnosperms?
c: plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary
flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits
the first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
the amphibians of the plant kingdom
items.e: Plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary: gymnosperms.

items.q: What is the ploidy of the endosperm in angiosperms?
items.e: It forms from the fusion of a male gamete with two polar nuclei.

items.q: Which fungi belong to Phycomycetes?
items.e: Phycomycetes: Rhizopus and Albugo.

items.q: What is heterospory?
c: producing two kinds of spores, large megaspores and small microspores
items.e: e.g. Selaginella and Salvinia; a step towards seeds.

items.q: Which group of plants is described as bryophytes?
c: the amphibians of the plant kingdom
the first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary
flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits
items.e: The amphibians of the plant kingdom: bryophytes.

items.q: Which agar-producing alga is used in growing microbes?
items.e: Agar is used in culture media and ice creams.

items.q: To which class of fungi do mushrooms, bracket fungi and smuts belong?
items.e: Basidiomycetes: mushrooms, bracket fungi and smuts.

items.q: To which class of fungi do Alternaria and Trichoderma belong?
items.e: Deuteromycetes: Alternaria and Trichoderma.

items.q: Which plants are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
items.e: The amphibians of the plant kingdom: bryophytes.

items.q: Which plants are called flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits?
items.e: Flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits: angiosperms.

items.q: Which is the dominant phase in pteridophytes?
items.e: The gametophyte is a small prothallus.

items.q: Which alga is a rich protein food supplement, even for space travellers?
items.e: It is unicellular and fast-growing.

items.q: Which group of plants is described as angiosperms?
c: the amphibians of the plant kingdom
plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary
the first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits
items.e: Flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits: angiosperms.

items.q: Which phylum has a water vascular system for movement and feeding?
items.e: It moves by many small water-filled tubes (podia).

items.q: Which animals show radial symmetry as adults?
items.e: Echinoderm larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

items.q: Which phylum shows the tissue level of organisation and cnidoblasts (stinging cells)?
items.e: Cnidaria: the tissue level of organisation and cnidoblasts (stinging cells).

items.q: Which class of vertebrates is cold-blooded and has a three-chambered heart, with moist skin?
items.e: Most reptiles also have three chambers, but dry scaly skin.
